text:
sara: quick thread — I'm putting a draft proposal in here for how we prioritize reserved pools + burst/preempt for the Dedicated launch. want sanity checks before i file a formal RFC.

miguel: +1, want to make sure we capture customer asks (esp. high-throughput finapps). can you call out quota semantics?

sara: yes — leaning toward two surfaces: 1) committed pool capacity (guaranteed) and 2) shared burst bucket with credit-based preemption. quotas would be per-account and per-pool.

deepa: how do we expect preemption to behave for latency SLOs? preempting long-running requests could harm p99.

owen: plan is preempt at allocation granularity, not mid-request. we keep existing request-level graceful-shutdown hooks and a short drain window (default 5s) for in-flight tokens. if a request is >5s we fallback to a cheaper model variant.

miguel: can we define credit rules? e.g., burst credits accumulate from unused committed capacity, expire in 30d, and are consumed by peak load. also support "reserve credits" bought monthly.

jenna: include business constraint — enterprise legal/risk wants guaranteed isolation for some customers, so "strict no-preempt" flag should be an opt-in on dedicated pools (higher price).

sara: agreed. so minimal policy draft: tier 0 = isolation (no preempt), tier 1 = committed with preempt safeguards, tier 2 = best-effort shared. defaults should be tier1.

deepa: what telemetry & launch gates do we need? propose: p50/p95/p99 latency for committed vs burst, preemption rate, failed requests due to preempt, and economic unit cost delta (tokens/$).

miguel: add rollout guard: <5% preempt rate on canary for 48h, and no >3 customer incidents tied to preemption in that window.

sara: launch criteria checklist (draft):
- API and console controls for pool tiering and "no-preempt" flag
- Billing visibility for committed vs burst usage
- Telemetry dashboards: preempt rate, tail latency, cost-per-token
- E2E smoke tests (canary traffic, simulated overload)
- Docs + pricing page updates

owen: ops constraints: autoscaler must support two knobs:
```
min_instances, max_instances, burst_capacity_ratio
```
We limit burst_ratio to 2x by default.

miguel: also need model-variant fallback policy in runtime to reduce p99 when heavy burst preemption occurs. recommend a "fallback profile" per pool.

deepa: SLA wording — we should be explicit: committed capacity has latency SLA; burst does not. but we need a degradation policy: when burst is used >X% for >Y mins we auto-escalate to capacity sales flow.

jenna: add negotiation point: early adopters can get higher burst caps for first 6 months with revenue commitment. sales needs that as a checkbox.

capacity-bot: created ticket PROD-2118 for "reserved-pools priority rules" and linked doc: https://go/restricted/PROD-2118

sara: next steps: i'll convert this into RFC draft by Friday. please reply here with any must-have constraints (security, billing, legal) — i'll fold into scope and call an async review. :sparkles:

owen: one more ops ask — include circuit-breaker on preempt actions to avoid cascading preempts across pools.

miguel: noted. i'll prototype credit accounting and expiry logic next week.

deepa: i'll draft the telemetry dashboard layout and alerts.

jenna: sales will prepare a checklist for early-adopter discounts and contract language.

sara: thanks team — filing RFC now and pinging infra/rev later.
